pitch_detail.notes: Easy climbing up pale slabs to a comfortable stance beneath a darker band of rock. Treat it as a warm-up and a chance to sort out the rope.
Follow an open book to its top, then move left across low-fifth-class ground to a talus-strewn bowl where the belay sits.
Take the rib on the right side of the bowl, with some scrambling mixed in, to a wide talus ledge. A long lead, so expect rope drag.

Crosses a very loose band of rock before reaching a gully with sounder stone. Little reliable protection and a lot of loose material; keep the second clear of the fall line. A weathered old cam was found around here, hinting at an earlier attempt.
Easy fifth-class going up the gully, ending at a secure belay.
More of the same gully, easy fifth-class ground.
Angle left to a left-facing corner and climb it to a good ledge on the prow.
Climb past one roof, up a ramp, and on to a second roof. A good ledge above serves as the belay.
A thin right-facing corner, then a short steep section, a ramp and a further corner lead to a big ledge.
Low-angle but loose face climbing ending at a poor belay.
Face climbing to a reasonable ledge; the anchor there takes some care to build. Run-out in places.
Keeps going up the face, finishing in the notch where the ridge shoulders out. Also run-out in places.
A short overhanging splitter crack, the hardest climbing on the route by grade, finishing on a loose ramp.
A varnished corner that relaxes into loose, mid-fifth-class terrain.
Traverse right to a ramp and follow it to the south ridge.
Scramble to the southwest summit.

review.changed: Wrote all 16 pitches from the first-ascent account (grades and lengths converted from feet). Single source; no bolt or anchor counts stated so none given. Crux assigned to the 5.10+ splitter pitch by grade. Pitch 4 old-cam note comes from the same account.
review.other_findings: Stored pitch count (16) and length agree. Source main text says five pitches of 5.10; pitch table lists 5.10 on 8, 9, 11, 12, 13.

pitch_detail.notes: Crack in a right-facing dihedral, mostly 5.4 with a couple of 5.6 moves. Protection is good, and the lead can use the whole rope. Late in the season the moat may only be crossable right at the base, over a small snow bridge.
Mostly fourth class, ending on a large grassy slope.
Reached after class 2-3 scrambling up a long left-trending ramp. Blocks and face climbing near the ridge crest end on a ledge.
A delicate traverse to the right with sparse protection, then a V-shaped grass and dirt constriction. One party reported being slightly left of the usual line here. Pitches of 40-50 m.
Easier ground than the one below, continuing toward the key ledge.
Reaches the key ledge, a common bivy spot.
A chimney with a small overhang and some loose blocks.
A short slab with nothing to protect it.
A short slab ending on a ledge. This and the previous pitch could be linked into one.
A deep, wide chimney to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote the pitch sequence as one party climbed it (10 pitches by their count). Grades only where stated; no lengths, bolts or anchors given. A second source (Mountaineers) mentioned a 5.5 chimney move near the summit and a .2 to #3 rack but could not be fetched in full, so it is not used for pitch notes.
review.other_findings: Stored pitch count is 9; the one account counts 10 and says it could be 9 if pitches 8 and 9 are linked. Descent in that account was about 13 single-rope rappels, not recorded in the stored row (rappels not in this wave).

skip_reasons.wa_argonaut_peak_east_ridge: Only route summaries found (8 pitches, 5.6, two single-rope rappels into the notch); no pitch-by-pitch account located.
skip_reasons.wa_bulls_tooth_south_ridge: Only one trip account, which describes nearly the whole roped section in a single 40 m pitch; stored count of 2 not supportable and no per-pitch detail.
skip_reasons.wa_dome_peak_indian_summer: Only a one-line summary (III 5.10, south face) found; no pitch descriptions beyond the stored beta.
skip_reasons.wa_dragontail_peak_boving_route: No source found describing this route at all.
skip_reasons.wa_dragontail_peak_colchuck_col_buttress: No source found describing this route at all.
